item.title: Giants outfielder suffers late-night scooter accident while already dealing with foot injury, team says
item.description: Harrison Bader's scooter accident further injured his foot as the San Francisco Giants outfielder prepares for an MRI while already battling plantar fasciitis.
item.content:encoded:
Harrison Bader's season has gone from bad to worse.

The San Francisco Giants outfielder has been limited to just 30 games due to injury, and when he's been on the field, it has not been pleasant.

Bader is hitting just .170 with a .198 on-base percentage and .358 slugging percentage, as he's dealt with plantar fasciitis for the second time in his MLB career.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

But this week, the Giants announced that Bader had a "scooter accident" on "Saturday night/early Sunday morning," which further injured his foot.

Bader is now set to get an MRI for the new injury.

Bizarrely enough, this is not the first time Bader has gotten into trouble with a scooter. While playing for the University of Florida in 2014, he was suspended for 19 games for drunkenly crashing a scooter into a parked truck.

MLB PROSPECT PROVIDES POSITIVE UPDATES AFTER FRACTURING VERTABRAE IN SCARY OUTFIELD COLLISION

Bader is in the first year of a two-year pact with the Giants, which is worth north of $20 million. The Giants are his seventh team.

The 2021 Gold Glove Award winner spent nearly six full seasons with the St. Louis Cardinals before being traded to the New York Yankees in 2022. He then had a brief stint with the Cincinnati Reds before spending time with the New York Mets, Minnesota Twins and Philadelphia Phillies.

The Giants, meanwhile, are tied for the second-worst record in the National League and figure to trade just about anyone they can ahead of next week's deadline.

item.title: Vacation paradise evacuated as raging wildfire threatens to roar back amid high winds
item.description: Strong winds threaten to reignite the Paros wildfire as tourists and residents share firsthand evacuation accounts from the popular Greek island.
item.content:encoded:
Greek authorities warned Wednesday that strong winds could reignite a wildfire on the popular tourist island of Paros, after the blaze forced residents and visitors to evacuate.

Paros, an island between Mykonos and Santorini, was hit by the wildfire Tuesday, prompting precautionary evacuations in multiple communities.

Flames spread through dry vegetation near the Kampi area, Italian outlet Ansa reported.

THOUSANDS SWARM STUNNING MOUNTAIN ESCAPE AS SELFIE TOURISM BACKLASH ERUPTS ONLINE

Although the blaze has since been largely contained, authorities are warning that strong winds could reignite lingering hot spots, the Greek City Times reported.

The winds could complicate firefighting efforts, the outlet said, and residents are being urged to avoid any activities that could spark fires.

As firefighters battled the blaze, local officials asked residents with available space to help house emergency crews working to contain the fire.

"The Municipality of Paros warmly thanks everyone who is responding in person at this difficult moment, supporting the forces that are fighting the flames." the translated statement read.

MAJOR CITY LAUNCHES HARSH TOURIST CRACKDOWN AS LOCALS REVOLT OVER MASSIVE CROWDS

Fox News Digital reached out to the Municipality of Paros for comment.

Known for its whitewashed villages and beaches, as well as its high-quality Parian marble, the island attracts visitors across the world. 

On a Reddit forum dedicated to travel in Greece, users shared concerns and firsthand accounts of evacuations as the wildfire spread across Paros.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

The commenters had been staying in Aliki and Parikia, two villages on the island, as well as the nearby island of Antiparos.

"We were staying near Aliki and had to evacuate," one person said. "Fire is pretty big now."

"I’m in Parikia at the moment. There are currently 4 choppers helping with the [wildfire], plus ground support," another Reddit user said. "They were filling up water right in front of the harbor and flew overhead my hotel."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

A third Reddit user said, "We’re in Antiparos now and it’s safe here. We could see the fires from our house last night. It looked really bad, but it seems like it’s almost gone now."

The Paros wildfire comes as Europe continues to battle a severe wildfire season.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Earlier this month, another major wildfire burned near Thessaloniki, Greece's second-largest city, due to record heat and dry conditions.

France and Spain have been hit by massive blazes in recent weeks, including the famed Fontainebleau Forest near Paris, where roughly 4,900 acres of woodland was burned.

While record-breaking heat has intensified the fire danger across Europe, experts say human activity, suspected arson and land management have also contributed to the devastating wildfire season.

Simon Constable contributed reporting.

item.title: JONATHAN TURLEY: Fauci took the Fifth—but his diary may have already answered for him
item.description: Senate hearing exposed diary entries where Fauci took credit for school closures he publicly denied, raising questions about his contradictions.
item.content:encoded:
"Stick with the science and never veer from that, even when the science turns out to be an inconvenient truth for somebody." Dr. Anthony Fauci, then Director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, delivered those words to Georgetown students in 2017 as the touchstone of medical ethics.

On Wednesday, before the Senate Homeland Security Committee, Fauci replaced that line by repeatedly saying, "On the advice of counsel, I respectfully decline to answer based upon my rights under the Fifth Amendment to the Constitution."

The optics could not have been worse, but what you saw depended largely on how you viewed the hearing. For critics, Fauci sounded like Crazy Joe Gallo without the sunglasses. For supporters, Fauci is still a hero who refused to fall into a trap laid for him. Democratic senators such as Sen. Maggie Hassan, D-N.H., actually praised Fauci for refusing to answer questions before Congress.

FAUCI PLEADS FIFTH WITH 'ZERO LEGAL JUSTIFICATION' AS CRITICS ERUPT AND DEMAND CONTEMPT CHARGES

There is no question that it is Fauci's right to invoke his privilege against self-incrimination, and many advised him to do so. The privilege can be invoked for strategic reasons separate from any criminal culpability. After all, he was given a last-minute pardon by President Joe Biden, and any false statements he made before the committee could be used to bring criminal charges against him.

However, Fauci is unlike many who have invoked the privilege. Unlike many past witnesses who have invoked it, Fauci has testified for days in countless prior hearings. He also has appeared in countless interviews on these issues. He had reason to fear this hearing after his diary revealed startling contradictions between his private observations and his public statements.

The question many will ask is why Fauci could not just "stick with the science" and resolve these contradictions. The fact is that he would have had difficulty dealing with his own "inconvenient truths."

FAUCI PRIVATELY TOOK CREDIT FOR COVID-19 LOCKDOWNS DESPITE PUBLIC DENIAL, NEWLY EXPOSED DIARY ENTRIES REVEAL

Fauci's opening statement expressed obvious anger over the release of his "unredacted diary."

The new evidence shows that Fauci connected the Wuhan lab to the emerging crisis before most people had ever heard of the lab. It also shows him repeatedly referencing the lab's gain-of-function work and discounting the "wet market" as the true origin of the virus, viewing it instead as an "amplifier."

Some of the most embarrassing areas for Fauci concerned his entries acknowledging that he pushed to close schools, despite public denials that he ever recommended such closures. His entries take credit for convincing figures such as then-New York City Mayor Bill de Blasio, the staff of California Gov. Gavin Newsom, and others to close schools.

FAUCI'S DIARY SHOWS HE FED QUESTIONS TO JOURNALISTS, BUILT FRIENDSHIPS WITH MEDIA FIGURES

In an Oct. 16, 2022, ABC interview, Fauci repeated that denial: "They always come back and say, 'Fauci was responsible for shutting schools down.' I had nothing to do [with it]!"

The media has also taken the Fifth on these subjects, declining to publish many of these contradictions. Media outlets have the same reason as Fauci: There is no spin that would reconcile their own prior coverage and gushing reviews of Fauci. The diary entries also show disturbing references to private meetings with media figures.

Fauci's diary refers to CNN anchor Jake Tapper 41 times. In some entries, Fauci suggested that the host was concerned about crafting an interview to better serve Fauci: "Jake wanted to make sure the interview did not cause me any problems." Fauci also related how he met socially with Tapper in July 2020: "Had dinner at Jake Tapper and Jen Tapper’s home in DC. Terrific couple. Friendship building." Notably, on Oct. 14, 2020, CNN published a report warning about the dangers of "small household gatherings."

The diary revealed an obsession with his publicity and access to celebrities. It is replete with Fauci’s gushing accounts of himself, such as, "It is not hyoperbole [sic] to say that today I am the most famous and talked about person in the country and one of the most recognizable peson [sic] in the world."

The fact is that diaries tend to be self-obsessed, and no one would want their unvarnished private thoughts made public. Rather, my gripe with these passages is one I have previously raised in criticism of Fauci. During this period, dissenting scientists were barred from social media, removed from positions, and vilified for expressing views, despite now being vindicated on subjects ranging from the lab origin of the virus to the efficacy of masks, the 6-foot rule, natural immunity and school closures.

As these courageous scientists were being abused by academic and media figures who still hold their positions, Fauci said not a word in their defense despite privately acknowledging that they could be right.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

Yet Fauci remained silent as his allies in the media savaged those who voiced the view that the virus was man-made and escaped from the lab.

In 2021, New York Times science and health reporter Apoorva Mandavilli was still calling on reporters not to mention the "racist" lab theory. Federal agencies found the lab theory to be the most credible, despite Fauci's public claim that a natural origin was the most likely explanation.

Fauci stayed silent while relishing his celebrity status. Indeed, his diary shows no concern for these scientists as he breathlessly recounted his bobbleheads and cover shoots.

Once again, Fauci has every right to invoke his constitutional rights, but the public has every right to demand answers to these questions related to the deaths of approximately 1.2 million to 1.25 million Americans. That may result in a grant of immunity to compel him to answer them.

If it is any solace to Fauci, he will clearly be able to maintain that he is "the most famous and talked about person in the country."

item.title: Coastal workers fleeing blue strongholds could create an opportunity for Detroit
item.description: Detroit locals and policy experts debate radical free-market reforms, including converting Belle Isle into a special economic zone to lure taxpayer flight.
item.content:encoded:
DETROIT — As high-tax, progressive-led cities continue to bleed residents nationwide, locals and policy experts in Detroit are offering contrasting visions for the Motor City’s future — with some eyeing radical free-market reforms to attract those fleeing the East and West coasts.

High state and local taxes, lingering crime concerns, and an astronomical cost of living continue to drive taxpayer flight out of blue strongholds like New York, Chicago, Boston, and Los Angeles. According to a study by the National Taxpayers Union Foundation (NTUF), taxpayers are consistently abandoning high-tax environments for fiscally friendly states. 

While Texas and Florida remain primary destinations, Sunbelt states like North Carolina, South Carolina, and Tennessee are seeing record population gains.

BLUE-STATE TAX BURDEN FUELS AMERICANS FLEEING TO REPUBLICAN-LED SOUTHERN STATES

For many moving away from major metros, the decision comes down to basic math.

"Cost of living is probably a huge reason for it. Those cities are some of the most expensive in the country," Ferndale resident Andy Femminineo told Fox News Digital on Monday.

Femminineo, who grew up in the Detroit suburbs and works downtown, noted that even high-earning tech workers are being priced out of coastal hubs.

"A lot of those people are showing up here in Detroit," he said. "The cost of living [on the coasts] is outstripping the tech talent they have there, which is ridiculous. I mean, it's humongous talent and income there, and you still can't afford to live."

Floyd Brantley, a born-and-raised Detroiter, sees the population shifts as part of a historical cycle for major urban centers.

"I think it's a nationwide trend, and what a lot of people don't realize is that cities are cyclical anyway," Brantley said. "This isn't the first upward swing that Detroit has been on. We've been up and down a few times. New York's been up and down a few times, Chicago — LA is losing a lot of people going to Texas."

DETROIT DEVELOPER CITES 'SUBSTANTIAL TAXES' AS REASON BIG BLUE CITIES LIKE NYC ARE IN TROUBLE

Former Detroit Planning Director Antoine Bryant echoed those sentiments, noting that the South and Midwest offer economic relief that coastal markets simply cannot match.

"The South in general has been growing tremendously," Bryant told Fox News Digital. "South Carolina has won, there's been tremendous growth in Texas as well, and you're seeing that along the coast because the income disparity isn't as vast as it is on the East and West coasts."

Bryant, who has lived in Detroit since 2021, expects the city to expand over the coming decade. "Many demographers and planners I talk to say there's real opportunity here in the Midwest," he added.

Other locals highlighted the permanent impact of remote work on traditional urban centers.

"People aren't working in the office buildings anymore, so they don't need to be centralized in major cities," said Allen Park resident Ashli Genaw, pointing to how flexible work policies allowed workers to leave New York and California.

While local residents remain hopeful about Detroit’s organic momentum, conservative policy thinkers argue that bolder action is required to capture fleeing taxpayers.

Rodney Lockwood, a board member at the Mackinac Center for Public Policy, believes major cities reliant on heavy tax bases are headed for trouble unless they embrace aggressive free-market alternatives.

"Right now, socialists are on the march, and perhaps [New York State Assemblymember] Zohran Mamdani is the best example of that. They're winning races, and their answer is always more taxes and more free stuff," Lockwood told Fox News Digital. "We have to look at both sides: what is not working, and then what will work."

DAVID MARCUS: IN BOOMING DETROIT, VOTERS SKEPTICAL OF SOCIALISM SNAKE OIL

Lockwood’s proposal? Convert Detroit’s iconic Belle Isle Park into an independent, free-enterprise "Freedom City" designed to compete directly with high-tax blue hubs.

Developed in the late 19th century, Belle Isle is a 982-acre island park sitting in the Detroit River — making it larger than New York City's Central Park. Under Lockwood’s vision, private investors would purchase the island from the city to build a mixed-use housing, entertainment, and commercial district structured as a special economic zone. The plan aims to accommodate 50,000 residents across 20,000 households without relying on public tax dollars.

"Detroit is stuck. Its population is not increasing fast enough, and it faces a potential fiscal cliff as federal COVID-relief money runs out," Lockwood argued.

However, the idea of privatizing Detroit’s prized public park met sharp resistance from several locals in the downtown area.

"Horrible idea," said Tanya Clark, a native Detroiter. "We need more public spaces throughout the city, not fewer. Other places might want that, but it's not a Detroit thing."

Others were more open to the ambitious concept.

"I think that’d be amazing," said Alonte Banks, a student living in downtown Detroit. "I’m pretty sure I’d move down there."

item.title: Top 5 moments from Fauci's hearing: Paul boots lawyer, Moreno erupts as contempt vote looms
item.description: Anthony Fauci invoked the Fifth Amendment 111 times during Rand Paul's Senate hearing, refusing to answer questions about gain-of-function research.
item.content:encoded:
What was billed as a battle of wits between Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., and Dr. Anthony Fauci, with the lawmaker determined to uncover the former COVID-19 explainer-in-chief’s motivations during the pandemic, became a one-sided affair in the Senate.

Paul has for years sought to uncover Fauci’s alleged role in funding "risky" research in China that Republicans say sparked the pandemic in 2020. He has argued that Fauci should be thrown in prison, and that the former chief medical advisor to the president’s pardon from former President Joe Biden wouldn’t hold up.

But the highly anticipated back and forth, which was further stoked by Paul dumping over 1,000 pages of Fauci’s diary online before the hearing, didn’t go exactly as planned.

The hearing kicked off with an impassioned opening statement from Paul, who accused Fauci and the National Institutes of Health (NIH) of funding gain-of-function research for years, misleading Congress and destroying records, which he contended created a fracture in public trust over the nation’s COVID-19 response.

"That loss of trust may be your most damaging legacy," Paul said. "Trust can't be ordered. It has to be earned. No scientist is above scrutiny. No government official beyond accountability, and no public servant preferred version of history."

RAND PAUL SEEKS CONTEMPT CHARGES AFTER FAUCI INVOKES FIFTH AMENDMENT MORE THAN 100 TIMES

But Fauci, under guidance from his lawyers, opted against answering any questions from Paul or others on the committee.

He argued that Paul's "obvious obsession" with pushing for his prosecution, levying allegations against him, and dumping his unredacted diary was designed to "get me to say something, anything, that could vindicate his repeated public pledges that I end up, in his words, quote, behind bars, unquote."

"Although it pains me to do so because of the respect I have for the legislative branch of government, and my decades-long record of cooperating with Congress under the advice of my attorneys, I will invoke my right under the Fifth Amendment of the Constitution to refrain from answering your questions," Fauci said.

It wasn’t long after Fauci invoked the Fifth Amendment that tensions flared in the hearing.

After being repeatedly asked questions, and repeatedly turning to his constitutional shield, Paul declared that as chair of the committee, he was denying Fauci’s right to invoke the Fifth Amendment.

"It's against the law to obstruct an investigation of Congress," Paul said. "There will be repercussions to your refusal to testify today."

WATCH: RAND PAUL SAYS THERE'S ONE THING AMERICANS HAVE NEVER HEARD FROM FAUCI

Then Fauci’s lawyer, David Schertler, spoke up to remind Paul it was Fauci’s constitutional right to turn to the Fifth Amendment.

Paul reminded Schertler that neither he, nor the "half dozen" lawyers with Fauci were recognized by the committee. That prompted Sen. Gary Peters, D-Mich., the top Democrat on the panel, to push for Schertler to speak.

But Paul was not having it.

"This is the way Anthony Fauci wants to be remembered — for a lawyer not listening to the rules," Paul said. "That's the way you want to be remembered, and that's what you're going to do. You are not recognized, sir. Security, please remove him from the room."

The hearing chugged along at roughly the same pace — lawmakers would ask Fauci a question, then he would invoke the Fifth Amendment.

But that didn’t stop some on the panel from getting frustrated at his lack of forthrightness.

Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, noted that Schertler was a well-known lawyer who previously represented former Sen. Bob Menendez, who was sentenced for accepting gold bars and bribes in exchange for using his influence to benefit the Egyptian government.

WATCH: RAND PAUL SAYS FAUCI LOBBIED FOR $1M PRIZE WHILE LEADING COVID RESPONSE

"And there's an article here in the Washington Free Beacon that talks about why you would hire a guy like David Schertler. And the comment is, if you're in deep s---, that's who you call," Moreno said. "Do you feel like you're in deep s---?"

Fauci again declined to answer, which prompted a frustrated Moreno to tell him that his influence over policy during the pandemic in 2020 and the effect that it had on Americans pushed him to run for the Senate.

"Here I am sitting in front of you six years later saying, ‘Who the f— do you think you were for doing that? It is a total disgrace what you did to this country,’" Moreno said.

As the hearing wound down, Paul revisited his threat to hold Fauci accountable for declining to answer questions.

Paul announced that he would seek contempt charges against Fauci after he invoked his Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination and teed up a vote in committee for next week.

"We're going to have a vote next week on contempt," Paul said. "I think there's another legal question that the courts may have to decide upon, and that is whether or not a presidential pardon offers you complete immunity."

Fauci never answered a question from any lawmaker on either side of the aisle, sticking to the advice from his lawyers to invoke the Fifth Amendment to protect himself from self-incrimination.

Before the hearing started, Paul and his staff were confident that Fauci wouldn't try to invoke the Fifth Amendment.

So confident, a source familiar with the matter told Fox News Digital, that several questions were prepared ahead of time, and members of the committee were told to come prepared.

In all, Fauci wound up uttering the same phrase 111 times: "On the advice of counsel, I respectfully decline to answer based upon my rights under the Fifth Amendment to the Constitution."

item.title: Willie Nelson urges Americans to fight 'water thieving' AI data centers devouring rural Texas farmland
item.description: Willie Nelson urges Americans to fight data centers invading rural Texas land, warning of light pollution and water thieving near his Abbott home.
item.content:encoded:
Willie Nelson urged Americans to think again when it came to building the future.

Nelson, 93, encouraged followers to "fight against data centers invading our land" in a social media plea shared Tuesday.

The country music legend reflected on being able to see "stars at night" in his Texas hometown, but that light pollution and "water thieving" were imminent in a looming industrial climate.

KACEY MUSGRAVES ABRUPTLY CANCELS CONCERT DATES FROM 'MIDDLE OF NOWHERE' TOUR

"I grew up in Abbott, and I still have a home there with farmed land where I can still see stars at night," Nelson told his followers.

"And now our community, like many others, needs to fight against data centers invading our land."

SINGER ZACH TOP SLAMS MODERN COUNTRY MUSIC, SAYS IT LACKS 'SOUL'

He added, "The last thing we need is a loud, water thieving, light polluting, data center anywhere near our town (or any others for that matter)."

The "On the Road Again" singer noted how "the strength of rural America has never come from big industrial footprints."

"It comes from generations of people, open spaces, local businesses, and a connection to the land," Nelson wrote. "All of America deserves thoughtful stewardship that doesn’t steal farmland (where our essential shared-food is grown) and small family farmers’ livelihoods, and not data centers that only destroy the environment around them."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

He added, "Whoever controls food and water, controls the masses. Let’s not allow our own demise or give up control over necessary resources in the U.S. and especially in Abbott."

Nelson's a longtime environmental advocate, and has raised more than $90 million through his Farm Aid nonprofit, which he cofounded with John Mellencamp and Neil Young more than four decades ago.

The charity was first formed in 1985 to raise awareness about the loss of family farms and to raise funds to keep farm families on the land.

On Tuesday, Gov. Greg Abbott called for a ban on data center developments in rural Texas.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"We must prohibit them from building AI data centers in rural Texas neighborhoods," he said on a campaign stop in Bullard, according to the Texas Tribune.

"I made clear already: Any AI data center even thinking about coming here — they got to bring their own money, bring their own power, reuse their own water and do it in a way that reduces the cost of electricity for residents across our state."

"We must eliminate the tax break they are getting. They must be responsible for funding their own projects here in Texas. We will get that done."

item.title: Top union 'cleared' by law firm over explosive corruption allegation previously gave millions to that firm
item.description: Pitta LLP received $11.6 million from the Hotel Trades Council and Unite Here Local 6 while investigating whistleblower corruption claims against them.
item.content:encoded:
A law firm that says it found no evidence to support corruption allegations against two New York City unions has long-running financial and familial ties to those labor organizations, public records show.

The Hotel Trades Council (HTC) and UNITE HERE Local 6 (UH6) hired Pitta LLP to investigate a whistleblower letter alleging a culture of quid pro quo corruption and improper gift-giving at the two unions. The firm’s review was completed in March 2026. While Pitta LLP ultimately found no evidence that the two labor organizations had broken the law, the firm had previously received millions from the unions. The firm's leaders also share family ties with former union leaders.

Some legal experts said this could lead to an appearance of impropriety.

Though the financial and familial relationships may raise eyebrows, Pitta LLP had no legal obligation to disclose them in its review.

SOURCES CORROBORATE WHISTLEBLOWER CLAIMS OF CORRUPTION, QUID PRO QUO CULTURE INSIDE POWERFUL NYC UNION

Between 2020 and 2025, HTC and UH6 collectively paid $11.6 million to Pitta LLP for legal services, an average of nearly $2 million a year, according to disclosure documents filed with the department.

The Center for Union Facts (CUF), a nonprofit watchdog group that is sharply critical of labor unions and union leadership, provided documentation to Fox News Digital showing that the father of Vincent Pitta, the law firm’s chairman, held leadership positions at the two unions and that his sister is married to Peter Ward, HTC’s former president. Pitta later confirmed both relationships in a statement to Fox News Digital.

Fox News Digital obtained and reviewed the preliminary statement from a second independent investigation conducted by a former state and federal prosecutor affiliated with a different law firm that also concluded that there was no evidence to support any of the allegations of misconduct set forth in the whistleblower letter.

"When confronted with information suggesting that employees, consultants, or other business partners have engaged in serious misconduct, most companies’ first reaction is to consult with a trusted outside firm with which the company has a long working relationship," the law firm Quinn Emanuel wrote in a 2022 publication. "But there are drawbacks to this approach. In a complex internal investigation, a company’s longtime corporate counsel can become subject to ethical conflicts, confirmation bias, divergent incentives and other issues that may produce a suboptimal result for the client."

Quinn Emanuel’s blog post relates to general legal ethics, not the facts of the relationship between Pitta LLP and the two labor unions.

"Companies facing potential criminal or regulatory investigations or any allegation of serious misconduct almost always will be better served by hiring counsel that does not have a long history of providing corporate or transactional advice to the company," the publication continued. "Even where the firm’s lawyers can acknowledge, for example, misconduct by the executives from whom the lawyers have taken instructions, confronting those issues creates tricky reputational and financial problems for the firm … the firm might fear that the company’s board of directors or other executives not implicated in misconduct will blame the firm, thereby jeopardizing the firm’s relationship with the company going forward."

UNIONS THAT PARALYZED NEW YORK COMMUTE OVER PAY SPENT MILLIONS ON LUXURY TRAVEL, FILINGS SHOW

The American College of Trial Lawyers, similarly, released guidance for internal investigations in 2020 which noted that government prosecutors "might be skeptical of an internal investigation of high-level or sensitive wrongdoing conducted by outside counsel regularly retained by the company" because "regular counsel may have a motive to avoid criticizing, and thus alienating, senior management, the source of past and future law firm revenues."

McKenna Long & Aldridge, another law firm, noted that engaging a firm with which an entity has "significant economic ties" presents "an obvious risk to independence" that must be weighed against the benefit provided by their familiarity with the case.

Pitta, in a statement to Fox News Digital, denied that financial and familial ties presented a conflict of interest when investigating the claims made against HTC and UH6.

"Our four-decade relationship with the unions, did not and does not constitute a conflict of interest as it relates to the expedited preliminary review conducted by one of our partners of the ‘anonymous allegations’ which you are interested in," he wrote. "We assiduously ‘call them, as we see them,’ to steal some baseball vernacular — without fear or favor."

Pitta said his firm charges the two unions a reasonable rate for its legal services.

"If the $12 million figure is accurate," he said, the average cost spread across the roughly 40,000 members of the unions would come out to just around "$1 per member per week for expert labor, employment, employee benefits, election law, and other requested legal services."

UTAH JUSTICE ALLEGEDLY SENT ‘INAPPROPRIATE’ TEXTS TO LAWYER IN KEY REDISTRICTING CASE, OFFICIALS LAUNCH PROBE

He also confirmed that his father, who passed away in 2005, held leadership positions at the two unions for roughly 30 years and that his sister is married to Ward. Pitta maintains that neither relationship constituted a conflict of interest and that, if it did, the firm would address it with the "highest ethical standards and the best practices of our profession."

Critics of organized labor, however, see things differently.

"Tapping the union's family firm doesn't exactly inspire confidence in the results," CUF communications director Charlyce Bozzello told Fox News Digital.

CUF has repeatedly targeted Richard Maroko, who serves as president of UH6 and HTC.

Sources familiar with the inner workings of UH6 and HTC previously told Fox News Digital that leadership at the two unions had what they described as an unusually close relationship with hotel management — a relationship they alleged allowed hotel owners to strike beneficial deals in exchange for information that helped union leaders retain their power.

The sources further alleged that individuals involved in hotel management provided union leaders with improper gifts, such as high-end food and drink, to build relationships with them.

An HTC spokesman previously flatly denied the underlying whistleblower claims, pointing to two investigations the union commissioned, including Pitta LLP’s March 2026 review, which found no evidence to support claims that hotel management was unusually close to union leadership or that union officials accepted improper gifts.

"Two exhaustive, independent investigations, including one by a former federal prosecutor, have concluded that these anonymous claims are frivolous, lack any factual basis, and were clearly an attempt to derail contract negotiations between the union and hotel management," HTC spokesman Austin Shafran previously told Fox News Digital. "Thankfully, these efforts failed as our union secured the best contract in its history that will provide unprecedented wage increases and benefits to tens of thousands of hotel workers. Nothing will ever deter the union from working every day to better the lives of our members and their families."

No HTC or UH6 leader, and no hotel executive allegedly involved in the whistleblower claims, has been charged with a crime or found to have engaged in professional misconduct in connection with the allegations.

HTC, which oversees UH6, did not respond to Fox News Digital’s questions about Pitta LLP’s financial and familial ties to the unions.

item.title: Former Democratic staffers, DEI leaders shape Smithsonian leadership amid political firestorm
item.description: A Fox News Digital review of biographies and social media profiles identified roughly two dozen people employed by the Smithsonian with ties to the left.
item.content:encoded:
As Republicans intensify scrutiny of the Smithsonian Institution, numerous former Democratic staffers and employees of progressive nonprofits are holding senior positions throughout the nonprofit, while officials responsible for hiring emphasized diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) initiatives. 

A Fox News Digital review of public biographies and social media profiles identified roughly two dozen individuals employed by the Smithsonian in leadership positions or as curators who worked for Democratic offices or progressive nonprofits before being hired. Leadership biographies and political donation records indicate the pattern extends beyond a handful of senior employees.

That former Democratic staffers and individuals previously employed by liberal nonprofits now hold leadership positions at the Smithsonian is likely to further fuel conservative criticism that the sprawling museum and research organization has developed a left-of-center bias.

TRUMP ORDERS SIGNS OUTSIDE SMITHSONIAN MUSEUM AMID ROW OVER ITS DEPICTION OF AMERICAN HISTORY

In recent weeks, Republicans have accused the Smithsonian, particularly its National Museum of American History, of promoting progressive ideology, emphasizing identity politics and giving insufficient attention to the nation’s founding and traditional historical figures. Republican lawmakers and the Trump administration also have criticized specific exhibits addressing gender identity, diversity and social justice, arguing that museum leaders have allowed political activism to displace the neutral presentation of history.

These allegations follow years of DEI-centric leadership.

Roshni Lal, the director of the Smithsonian’s office of academic appointments and internships, which oversees academic hiring and internships, has had a career-long commitment to advancing DEI in hiring, professional biographies show.

Lal previously was the director of diversity, equity and inclusion for the Mountain Pacific Association of Colleges & Employers, where she oversaw policies, training and programming she characterized as anti-racist and rooted in social justice, according to her Smithsonian biography. She also held DEI-related roles at the Manhattan Beach Chamber of Commerce and the National Association of Colleges and Employers before joining the Smithsonian, per Lal’s LinkedIn page.

In a 2024 podcast appearance, Lal discussed her dedication to "identity-based career services," partially through connecting with "students of color" through "culturally inclusive" job placement.

Public Smithsonian biographies show that several curators at the National Museum of American History describe their work as focusing on race, identity and social justice, themes that also appear in a number of the museum's exhibits and initiatives.

WATCH: ‘SHOCKING’ BEN FRANKLIN SMEAR LEAVES SMITHSONIAN CHIEF WITH ‘NO REGRETS’

The current chairwoman of the National Museum of American History political history division, which is responsible for overseeing exhibits about American presidents, for instance, also oversees the Smithsonian’s Center for Restorative History, which says on its website that it exists to "spotlight the people and stories that have been excluded from our national narrative using the principles of restorative justice" by bringing together "diverse voices."

Among the center’s flagship programs are an effort to preserve the history of the Black Lives Matter movement by centering the perspectives of activists and a "decolonization working group," according to its website.

Multiple other curators at the National Museum of American History approach their jobs with a similar focus on racial identity, per their Smithsonian biographies. These include one curator who is working on "stitching social justice throughout the Americas" through their exhibit work as well as multiple scholars who primarily study race.

While Lal started her role at the Smithsonian in November 2023, her predecessor, who held the position for 11 years beginning in 2012, previously worked for the Clinton White House, the Obama State Department and as a special assistant to then-Sen. Hillary Clinton, according to his LinkedIn profile.

Lal did not respond to a request for comment when reached by Fox News Digital Tuesday.

"The Smithsonian is a nonpartisan institution, and politics does not factor into our hiring practices," a spokesperson for the institution told Fox News Digital. "Our hiring is solely based on qualifications to fulfill the responsibilities of any given position."

Leadership at the Smithsonian is not monolithic. The institution’s chief legal officer worked in the Bush administration, and the chief of staff to the organization's regents clerked for Chief Justice John G. Roberts on the Supreme Court as well as Justice Brett Kavanaugh during his time on D.C.'s federal appellate court, according to their institutional biographies.

DEI HIRING BOOST FOR ONE BLUE STATE'S MUSLIM COMMISSION INITIATIVE FLIES IN FACE OF TRUMP'S ANTI-WOKE PUSH

Congressional Republicans held two hearings to investigate allegations that the Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History has used taxpayer money to promote left-wing narratives about race, gender and oppression while minimizing the nation’s founding ideals and achievements. Following the hearings, conservative lawmakers are expected to be using Congress’ spending authority in an attempt to restrict Smithsonian funding to pressure it to remove exhibits they feel are inappropriate.

"These leaders have commandeered an institution that the nation entrusted to them to ensure the transmission and, thus, continuance of American culture and heritage and have perversely turned it into its opposite, a hothouse for anti-American activism," Heritage Foundation senior fellow Mike Gonzalez said during his July 21 congressional testimony on the Smithsonian. 

"These leaders often reveal, in their own words, that they see the world in terms of power dynamics — who has dominance and how to wrest it from them by dismantling the American narrative, all deeply Marxist and Gramscian constructs."

Other senior Smithsonian staffers who came from left-of-center backgrounds, according to LinkedIn profiles and other online biographies, include the National Museum of American History head librarian, who previously worked for the liberal Urban Institute; an advisory board member who was a senior staffer for the late Sen. Dianne Feinstein; the institution’s undersecretary for education, who served as the deputy assistant secretary of education during the Obama administration; the Smithsonian’s associate director of advancement for strategic initiatives, who came from the NAACP; and the director of communications for the National Museum of American History, who worked as a senior staffer for House Democratic leadership before joining the institution.

Curators with liberal backgrounds, per LinkedIn profiles and online biographies, meanwhile, include the recently departed director of curatorial affairs at the National Portrait Gallery, who held multiple DEI-related positions at colleges; an associate curator at the National Museum of the American Indian who was involved with a militant civil rights organization in the 1970s, the American Indian Movement; and a curator of time-based media for the Smithsonian American Art Museum who previously worked for a feminist art gallery.

Fox News Digital considered groups that publicly align with the Democratic Party or those that focus on issues such as environmentalism, racial justice or left-of-center economic policy as liberal for the purposes of its review.

The Smithsonian has roughly 6,400 full-time employees with varying degrees of public documentation. Fox News Digital's review covered a relatively small slice of that total, focusing on publicly identified leadership at the top of the institution as well as leaders at the National Museum of American History and individuals identifying themselves as curators on LinkedIn.

While a full accounting of the political beliefs of the Smithsonian’s senior staff and curators is impossible to glean from public records alone, political donations can provide some insight.

Only about 1% of donations made by individuals identifying themselves as Smithsonian employees have gone to Republican committees this cycle, according to campaign finance records reviewed by Fox News Digital.

Fox News Digital reached each Smithsonian employee mentioned for comment.

item.title: Mamdani won't rule out cash reparations, says he'll await NYC commission findings
item.description: Zohran Mamdani did not rule out cash reparations for Black New Yorkers when pressed during an interview, saying he awaits the commission's findings.
item.content:encoded:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani did not rule out awarding cash reparations to people impacted by slavery in the Big Apple during an interview on Tuesday, but said he was looking forward to the release of the findings by the city's commission.

"If a commission studying reparations in this city recommended cash reparations for people impacted in New York City, would you support that recommendation?" Charles Blow asked Mamdani during an interview for "The Root."

Blow also noted Mamdani's statement from when he was running for mayor that read, "New York City participated actively in the slave trade and furthered its legacy through racist institutions, policies, and laws. The city should reconcile and repair this legacy of slavery, stolen wealth and discrimination."

NEW YORK FAR-LEFT GROUP CLAIMS REPARATIONS 'OWED' AS BLACKS' MEDIAN WEALTH 'NEARLY 15 TIMES LESS' THAN WHITES

"First, I want to say that I stand by what I submitted. It’s the truth. It’s not a personal assessment. And we often think about slavery and the complicity in slavery as being exclusively to certain geographic areas of the country. Here in New York City, we were very complicit. So I look forward to whatever those findings are. I can’t give you an answer in advance of them, but I can tell you that this is critically important because this is also what it looks like to acknowledge what history truly was," Mamdani responded.

The New York City Commission on Racial Equity (CORE) was established in 2024 under Local Law 92 "to study how NYC government contributed to slavery and the harms caused by its legacies," according to the commission's website. A separate process for "Truth, Healing and Reconciliation" was established under Local Law 91 and allows "New Yorkers a way to publicly acknowledge the history and harm of slavery and its legacies in New York City, and the harms caused by it," the website reads.

According to the schedule on CORE's website, the commission are expected to release their final report for the "Truth, Healing and Reconciliation Planning Process" in June of 2027. The final report on the reparations study is expected in July of 2027 and the implementation for the "Truth, Healing and Reconciliation" plan is expected by June 18, 2028.

MAMDANI ALLOCATES $500K FOR REPARATIONS TALKS AS NYC FACES $5.4B DEFICIT

"We would like to thank the Mayor for using his platform to acknowledge New York City's complicit history in chattel slavery. New York was home to the second-largest slaveholding population in America, after Charleston, South Carolina. The first commodities traded on Wall Street included the buying and selling of enslaved Black people, and their brutal forced unpaid labor built one of the most powerful economic engines in the world. Recognizing this history is an important step toward understanding the enduring legacy of slavery and its impact on our city and nation," Linda Tigani, chair and executive director of NYC CORE, told Fox News Digital in a statement.  

The statement continued, "We must repay the longstanding debt owed and truly tackle the racial wealth gap in New York City which is directly correlated to the stain of slavery in New York City. Since the passing of Local Law 91 and 92, the NYC Commission on Racial Equity has reached thousands of New Yorkers to formulate recommendations to pay the debt and advance permanent structural change to end racist practice in our city." 

The commission rebuked Mamdani after the mayor released his Preliminary Citywide Racial Equity Plan in April, and said in a press release that it failed to meet the requirements of the NYC charter.

"At a moment when communities across the country are deeply concerned about the direction of racial justice and equity under Donald Trump’s national political climate, New Yorkers made clear through our five-borough town halls that city government has a responsibility to lead with accountability and investments in communities most impacted by inequity," Tigani said at the time.

CHAOS ERUPTS AT NY REPARATIONS HEARING AS ‘FOUNDATIONAL’ BLACK AMERICANS CLASH WITH LEFT-LEANING GROUPS

CORE's findings say community members feel that Mamdani's plan fails to include a meaningful citywide racial equity strategy, required race-disaggregated data standards, neighborhood-level accountability metrics, a clear response to community racial equity priorities, and transparent funding tied directly to racial equity outcomes.

The commission has hosted rallies and gatherings in the city, including one for Juneteenth this year, which Forbes reported was the city's largest reparations gathering yet.

"The goal of the event for NYC CORE was to create a space where joy, community, and civic engagement were at the center of both commemorating Juneteenth and advancing the conversation around reparations and racial equity," political strategist Tyrik Washington, who partnered with CORE to aid a study on reparations in New York City, told the outlet in June.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Washington added, "If reparations policies were implemented in New York City today, I believe that within five to ten years we would see measurable reductions in occupational segregation and meaningful progress toward pay equity for Black New Yorkers."

A progress update report was released by CORE in January, touting $500,000 "committed to community groups in 2026 to participate in a Reparations, Truth, Healing, and Reconciliation Network."

The report detailed how more than two dozen groups would be given tens of thousands of dollars each to participate in "conversations to discuss the development of a Reparations study" and to gather "input on the early development of the citywide Truth, Healing and Reconciliation plan."

Funding, according to the document, "allows for each community member to receive an incentive for their time" and covers the costs of providing participants with "refreshments."

item.title: PGA TOUR picks: Six Rocket Classic 2026 best bets ready to attack the Detroit Golf Club's tougher greens
item.description: Hideki Matsuyama, Akshay Bhatia and Davis Thompson headline golf betting picks for the eighth and final Rocket Classic at Detroit Golf Club.
item.content:encoded:

Debuting in 2019, the event has produced champions such as Bryson DeChambeau, Rickie Fowler and two-time winner Cam Davis, but Rocket Mortgage will not return as title sponsor in 2027.

Detroit Golf Club’s renovated Donald Ross layout has been transformed into a 7,328-yard, par-70 test. Two former par-5s are now lengthy par-4s, while rebuilt greens, repositioned bunkers and more challenging green complexes should place a greater premium on accurate approach play and scrambling.

Last week, 21-year-old Jackson Koivun held off Scottie Scheffler to win the 3M Open by three strokes in just his third professional start. Koivun now joins a loaded Detroit field featuring Cameron Young, Xander Schauffele, Patrick Cantlay, Hideki Matsuyama, Russell Henley and Chris Gotterup.

JACKSON KOIVUN ARRIVES IN STYLE, LUCAS GLOVER TAKES OFF HIS SHOES, AND THE GREATEST GOLF DAD MOMENT

Miraculously, I won money at last week's 3M Open thanks to four of my five guys cashing placement bets. After banking +3.35 units (u) at the 3M Open, my 2026 PGA TOUR balance is at -50.18u. This week, I'm allocating 2.11u on six guys to win outright and backing them up with 2.75u worth of placements. Here are my picks for the Detroit Golf Club.

Rocket Classic 2026 betting card

The following odds are based on my previous bets on the golfers listed below. Subject to change.

🇯🇵 Hideki Matsuyama +3678 at Polymarket (0.55u) and Top-10 with ties +295 at Kalshi (0.5u)

🇺🇸 Ryan Gerard +4662 at Polymarket (0.43u) and Top-10 with ties +295 at Kalshi (0.5u)

I’m going back to the well on Hideki after he cashed a top-10 ticket last week by tying for third at the 3M Open. The driver has been the weakest club in the bag this season, but he’s gained strokes off-the-tee (OTT) in his last three tournaments.

TONY ROMO'S BRUTAL GOLF SCORE BEFORE GETTING ARRESTED PAINTS A NIGHTMARISH PICTURE

Surprisingly, Matsuyama lost strokes on approach last week, and he is one of the best iron players in the world. In fact, Hideki led the field in Strokes Gained (SG): Approach at last year’s Rocket Classic, and he’s gained strokes with his irons in four of his five career visits to the Detroit Golf Club.

Matsuyama has a world-class short game, which will be more important this week at the Detroit Golf Club due to the offseason renovations that made the green complexes tougher.

Furthermore, Hideki has gained strokes on the field putting in six of his last seven starts. Ultimately, if Matsuyama has another good week driving the ball, he should be a top-five betting favorite at the Rocket Classic.

According to Betsperts Golf, Gerard is third in total strokes gained over the last 24 rounds. He has three top-10 finishes over that span: T10 at the Charles Schwab Challenge, second at the Memorial Tournament and T9 at The 154th Open Championship.

Gerard has gained strokes putting in his last six starts, per DataGolf.com, with his driver in five straight, and around-the-green in four straight. Colonial Country Club, the host course of the Charles Schwab, is another Par 70 that’s a good tee-to-green (T2G) test with Bentgrass greens.

The Memorial is a "signature event" with a world-class field played at another Midwest course with Bent greens, and Gerard led the field in putting that week. The T9 at the British Open in his last start was Gerard’s second-best finish in a major.

He is close to breaking through for his first career win in a PGA TOUR regular-season event (he won the 2025 Barracuda Championship, an opposite-field event), and I have a hunch Gerard will play well this week.

There is little danger from T2G at the Detroit Golf Club, and Bhatia has one of the best short-games on TOUR. In fact, he leads the TOUR this year in SG: Putting, and he ranks third in this field in SG: Short-game (chipping and putting) over the last eight months, according to Betsperts Golf.

The biggest change to the Detroit Golf Club this offseason is to the greens, and if I trust anyone to learn these new greens, it’s the leader in SG: Putting. Bhatia’s short-game is so good that he won the 2026 Arnold Palmer Invitational, another "signature event," despite losing strokes to the field in ball-striking (driving and approach).

Meanwhile, Akshay should’ve, could’ve won the 2024 Rocket Classic, but he three-putted on the final hole to lose by a stroke. Bhatia finished T26 in last year’s Rocket Classic because he was 137th in SG: Around-the-Green and 104th in SG: Putting.

However, Akshay ranked eighth in SG: T2G last year, and has gained strokes ball-striking in his three Rocket Classics. If he can marry his career ball-striking at the Detroit Golf Club with his short-game from this season, Bhatia could get his second win of the year.

This is a "gut feeling" bet because Keegan is a proven winner who’s gotten at least one win in the past four years. Two of those wins are the 2023 and 2025 Travelers Championships, which were played at a comp course (TPC River Highlands) to the Detroit Golf Club.

Also, while this year’s Rocket Classic field is the strongest in the tournament’s history, last year’s Rocket Classic field wasn’t that much weaker and Bradley closed at +2000. Albeit he was playing much better last year, and won the 2025 Travelers a week before.

Regardless, Bradley has made the cut in his five career Rocket Classics, and he has gained strokes with his irons in eight consecutive starts, including the last three majors and three signature events, and is underrated ARG.

Meaning, Keegan is familiar with this place, is hitting the ball well lately, and his crafty short-game could be useful given the renovations to the Detroit Golf Club’s greens.

Before breaking through for his first PGA TOUR win at the 2024 John Deere Classic, Thompson finished T9 at the U.S. Open and T2 at the Rocket Classic in the two lead-in tournaments.

Pinehurst Resort, the host of the 2024 U.S. Open, is also a Donald Ross course, like the Detroit Golf Club, and the John Deere is a similar tournament setup as the Rocket Classic. As in, they have similar fields and are both played in the Midwest at the same time on the calendar.

Maybe his T7 at last week’s 3M Open is a sign that Thompson is ready to win again. The 3M Open is another Midwest tournament at an easy course, like the Rocket Classic. Plus, he is third in this field for average strokes gained at Donald Ross courses over the last three years, per Betsperts Golf.

I’m taking a shot with Thompson at this price because he has all the talent in the world and is still just 27-years-old. Lastly, the sharp money is on his +7094 odds. Bookmaker, the sharpest sportsbook in the golf betting market, has Thompson’s odds at roughly 60-to-1.

All the models I built for the 2026 Rocket Classic have many driving stats because Detroit Golf Club is an easy "bomber’s paradise". That said, Svensson is seventh in my 40-round model at Bet The Number because he ranks third in this field for SG: OTT, 10th in driving distance and 13th in birdie-or-better rate.

The Swede finished T9 at THE CJ CUP Byron Nelson five starts back and T4 at the 2026 RBC Canadian Open three starts back. The host courses of those two events are similar to the Detroit Golf Club; both are driver-heavy courses with Bentgrass greens.

item.title: Shark Week puts shark bite survival in focus with ER doc's expert tips
item.description: An emergency physician reveals the tourniquet and pressure dressing steps that determine survival in the first five minutes after a shark attack.
item.content:encoded:
While shark encounters are exceedingly rare, an unexpected bite can pose an immediate, life-threatening emergency.

In the critical first five minutes following an attack, swift action is the single biggest factor in survival.

Dr. Kenneth J. Perry, an emergency medicine physician based in South Carolina, broke down the vital steps bystanders and victims should take to manage the situation before professional medical care arrives.

SHARK WEEK SHOCKER AS GREAT WHITE BREACHES JUST YARDS FROM OBLIVIOUS BOOGIE BOARDER

The first step is to get the victim onto land or a boat to prevent further bites and avoid drowning. Once out of the water, the focus can shift to bleeding control.

"Shark bites vary in intensity and severity, but the main issue that all of them share is the need to stop the bleeding," Perry told Fox News Digital.

Because shark teeth can easily tear through major arteries, veins and tendons, uncontrolled blood loss is the biggest immediate threat.

10-FOOT GREAT WHITE SHARK SPOTTED SWIMMING DANGEROUSLY CLOSE TO YOUNG PEOPLE

For severe limb injuries, it's essential to apply a tourniquet, but many people fail to apply sufficient pressure. The tourniquet must be placed above the wound and tightened to the point where a pulse can no longer be felt, according to Perry.

For example, if a victim is bitten near the elbow, the tourniquet must be placed around the upper bicep and tightened until the pulse at the wrist disappears completely.

"It may be painful, but it is necessary," Perry noted.

This aligns with national trauma protocols from the American College of Surgeons' Stop the Bleed initiative, which emphasizes that effective tourniquet placement requires firm, tight compression to fully stop arterial blood flow.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Tourniquets are temporary tools and should be used for as short a duration as possible, Perry cautioned. There is a maximum window of about two hours before tissue damage occurs from lack of oxygenated blood flow.

If someone is stranded in a remote area and immediate emergency transport is unavailable, Perry recommends using a pressure dressing.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

This involves folding gauze multiple times, placing it directly over the specific point of bleeding, and wrapping it tightly. While a pressure dressing does not eliminate blood loss as completely as a tourniquet, it carries a much lower risk of tissue necrosis (death) during prolonged waits.

Bystanders play a crucial role beyond physical first aid by helping the victim stay motionless and quiet. Panic increases heart rate and blood pressure, which accelerates blood loss, the doctor noted.

Loss of consciousness after a shark attack can have more than one cause, Perry said.

A sudden drop in blood pressure and the body's stress response may trigger fainting. If the victim was deep underwater and surfaced too quickly during the attack, unconsciousness could signal a pressure-related diving injury, such as arterial gas embolism or barotrauma, which requires emergency treatment.

While controlling blood loss is crucial in the first five minutes, long-term recovery involves fighting off severe marine bacteria.

Aquatic bites are notorious sources of aggressive skin and soft-tissue infections like cellulitis, Perry warned.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Once a patient is resuscitated with fluids and blood products at a medical facility, aggressive antibiotic treatment usually follows.

item.title: ICE arrests more than 900 suspected human traffickers during FIFA World Cup, rescues 180 victims: DHS
item.description: DHS says more than 900 suspected human traffickers were arrested and 180 victims rescued during the 2026 FIFA World Cup, including 30 children.
item.content:encoded:
Federal agents arrested more than 900 suspected human traffickers and rescued 180 victims — including 30 children — during the 2026 FIFA World Cup, the Department of Homeland Security announced Wednesday.

The 905 arrests came during operations led by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement's Homeland Security Investigations, working alongside the DHS Center for Countering Human Trafficking and federal, state and local law enforcement agencies, DHS said.

"While Americans and international visitors were enjoying the FIFA World Cup, the men and women of ICE law enforcement were hard at work cracking down on human trafficking operations in FIFA host cities across the country," DHS Assistant Secretary Lauren Bis said in a statement. 

"Federal law enforcement arrested more than 900 suspects and rescued nearly 200 victims. Under President Trump and Secretary Mullin, we are dismantling human trafficking networks."

ELEVEN INDICTED IN ALLEGED TEXAS SMUGGLING SCHEME THAT LEFT 7 MIGRANTS DEAD IN SHIPPING CONTAINER

One of the biggest cases unfolded Friday in Dallas, where HSI agents arrested eight people accused of running an adult bookstore that investigators said had secretly operated as a brothel for more than 20 years.

The investigation began in 2023 and found that thousands of adults and children were allegedly sold for sex through the business, according to DHS. Investigators identified dozens of victims. One victim was murdered in 2024, and a defendant in that case was later convicted and sentenced to life in prison.

The eight suspects face charges that include conspiracy to commit sex trafficking, sex trafficking by force, fraud and coercion and money laundering conspiracy. The case is being prosecuted by the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Northern District of Texas.

FBI BOSS KASH PATEL DETAILS HOW AGENCY AND PARTNERS SECURED RECORD-SHATTERING FIFA WORLD CUP

In another case, HSI agents in San Francisco, working with the FBI and local police, rescued two girls believed to be victims of human trafficking. One of them had been missing from Bakersfield, California, since November 2025, according to DHS.

The trafficking cases were part of a broader security effort during the World Cup.

DHS also said its agencies seized more than 700 unauthorized drones, inspected more than 19,000 vehicles headed to stadiums and fan festivals and confiscated hundreds of thousands of counterfeit World Cup merchandise items worth more than $33 million.

item.title: House progressives revive Green New Deal for public schools as Dem civil war empowers far left
item.description: Rep. Pramila Jayapal is leading progressives in introducing a Green New Deal for public schools, legislation that has little chance of passing.
item.content:encoded:
The environmental and social justice movement behind the Green New Deal is back at the forefront of Democrats' agenda, this time targeting America's education system.

A group of House progressives led by Rep. Pramila Jayapal, D-Wash., introduced a bill this week to "establish a Green New Deal for public schools."

Details of the bill are not immediately available, and Jayapal's office did not respond to a Fox News Digital request for more details.

FAR-LEFT ACTIVIST CONFERENCE AT TEACHERS UNION HQ RAISES CLASSROOM CONCERNS

But a similar bill introduced five years ago by controversial ex-Rep. Jamaal Bowman, D-N.Y., entailed investing hundreds of billions of dollars into grants for public schools to make clean energy upgrades while also promoting curriculum changes focused on social and environmental equity.

Grants under that 2021 legislation would have also been aimed at "development of place-based and experiential education and community-driven curricula, with a focus on curricula that affirm and explore the underlying principles of the Green New Deal, including the significance of and the connections between racial, economic, and environmental and climate justice."

Grant funding would also be marked for "diversifying the workforce" and "expanding social service programming."

CONTROVERSIAL TEACHER TRAINING TARGETS PARENTAL AUTHORITY AS OPPRESSION, EDUCATION EXPERT WARNS

Pushing a "Green New Deal for schools" is also a focus of the far-left political organization The Sunrise Movement, which is dedicated to electing progressive lawmakers and counts fighting Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) among its non-climate-focused goals.

Rep. Tim Walberg, R-Mich., chairman of the House Committee on Education and the Workforce, panned the legislation when reached by Fox News Digital.

"The best way to prepare the next generation is by strengthening core academics, not expanding ideological programs. Parents and taxpayers have every right to expect schools to stay focused on education," Walberg said.

The resurgence of a Green New Deal push by progressives comes amid a growing civil war within the Democratic Party.

Self-proclaimed democratic socialists and candidates affiliated with them are challenging — and in some cases defeating — establishment Democrats in primaries across the country.

item.title: What happened to leaving the groom at the altar like an adult? Bride-to-be accused of setting fire to church
item.description: A Utah bride-to-be allegedly started a fire in the church the day before her wedding using a stolen lighter and a tampon, causing over $108,000 in damage.
item.content:encoded:
The erosion of societal standards can be found just about anywhere you look these days. That includes backing out of a trip down the aisle you're not looking forward to taking.

There used to be a time when an honest conversation could be had. An engagement could be called off well before the wheels are set in motion on putting together a wedding.

Even if you got caught up in the excitement of being engaged, realized you weren't with the one you wanted to marry, but, for whatever reason, never got around to calling it off, there was a solid backup plan.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON’T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

You could always not show up to your own wedding. Leaving someone at the altar isn't ideal by any means, but it's far less destructive than, let's say, attempting to burn down the church the day before the wedding.

It's far less criminal of an option. In fact, there are a lot of pros to leaving the groom at the altar like an adult.

A 25-year-old bride-to-be in Utah is now facing arson charges after being accused of starting a fire in the church she was scheduled to get married in the next day.

Lenita "Tessa" Joy Moreno was arrested on Monday. Court documents state that she, the groom-to-be, and family members were setting the church up on July 10 for their wedding when the fire alarm went off.

WEDDING HORROR STORIES GO VIRAL, ARE EQUAL PARTS DISTURBING AND HILARIOUS

Water from wedding decorations and a fire extinguisher were used to put the fire out. Investigators determined that the fire appeared to have been started under a chair with the help of a tampon.

Prior to the fire, the couple had gone to the Relief Society room, where the fire started. They were allegedly securing the building.

"It is believed that Lenita (Tessa) started a fire within a church building while 5 others were still inside," according to the probable cause affidavit, reports KUTV.

"Lenita did not obtain a marriage license for her own wedding that was to occur the following day after the fire but had lied stating she had."

During the investigation, the groom mentioned that they had gone to a hardware store earlier that day. When they reviewed security footage at the hardware store, investigators said Moreno stole two or three lighters.

The groom was reportedly not near her during her alleged theft. She also allegedly admitted during an interview to stealing from the store, but refused to say what she stole.

Moreno is reportedly facing multiple charges, including first-degree aggravated arson, misdemeanor retail theft and providing false information to a peace officer.

The fire caused more than $108,000 in damage to the church building. How good does leaving someone at the altar look right about now?

item.title: Alabama basketball coach Nate Oats marries former hoops staffer 20 years his junior following divorce
item.description: Nate Oats married former Alabama basketball staffer Alex Accetta last weekend, with several Crimson Tide coaches and AD Greg Byrne attending.
item.content:encoded:
Valentine's Day may be long gone, but love is definitely in the air.

Alabama head basketball coach Nate Oats, 51, and former staffer Alex Accetta, 31, tied the knot last weekend in a ceremony attended by several Crimson Tide coaches as well as athletic director Greg Byrne.

Accetta worked as the team’s director of operations before leaving for a role with the NBA’s Dallas Mavericks in guest experience and operations.

FORMER NEBRASKA WOMEN'S BASKETBALL COACH ADMITS SEXUAL RELATIONSHIP WITH EX-PLAYER, LAWSUIT CLAIMS

Oats revealed that he and Accetta were engaged back in April.

The wedding comes after a quiet divorce between the Alabama basketball coach and his ex-wife, Crystal Oats, back in 2023.

item.title: Bears legend Brian Urlacher talks team's likely move, USC son's college career
item.description: Brian Urlacher says the Chicago Bears' Hammond, Indiana stadium move is a ploy, while his son Kennedy thrives at USC after transferring from Notre Dame.
item.content:encoded:
Brian Urlacher is calling his former team's bluff.

The Chicago Bears have gone on record to say they are moving from the Windy City to Hammond, Indiana, announcing in June that they were "advanc[ing]" their stadium project in the city.

But Urlacher is still holding onto hope in at least staying in the state of Illinois.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"I think that was still a ploy to try to get the state of Illinois to do something more than what they’ve done, which is nothing," Urlacher said to Fox News Digital recently. "The Bears bought the land in Arlington Heights. They have that there, ready to go. They just need a little bit of funding from the state to build the stadium.

"I just cannot see the Bears leaving Illinois. It drives me crazy. And I don’t want them leaving Soldier Field, honestly. I wish they could work something out to keep them there, but they want a dome, they want Super Bowls, they want Final Fours. They want all that big stuff. I get it. I just hate the fact that they’re leaving Soldier Field. That place is iconic."

"I understand Indiana is offering them some great deals tax-wise — $2.5 billion to build the stadium. That’s a big deal. As a businessperson, which the owners have to be these days, it makes sense to go. Unless Illinois comes through with something, I don’t see them staying there," he added.

Perhaps Urlacher's son, Kennedy, can be a Hammond legend – he is currently a safety at USC after playing his freshman season with Notre Dame. He played in the national championship with the Fighting Irish, but it was time to move on.

"NIL has been great for him," Urlacher admitted. But the Urlachers also knew Kennedy would be a starter with the Trojans.

Perhaps the last name helped Kennedy get some more money, but Dad said Kennedy wants to earn everything on his own.

CHICAGO BEARS LEGEND BRIAN URLACHER SLAMS ILLINOIS DEMOCRATS AS TEAM PREPARES TO LEAVE STATE

"I’ll tell you what he does: He busts his a--. I don’t care what his name is. His name could be Johnson. It doesn’t matter. This dude plays hard. He works his tail off, man. Every time I call him, he’s working out, he’s doing something. He doesn’t want anything given to him because of his last name. That’s not why he wants to be where he’s at. He wants to be there because he earned it, because he busted his a-- and he got there..." Urlacher said.

"He wants nothing because of his last name. He wants it because he earned it."

Urlacher said, despite not liking what NIL has done to college sports, that he obviously wishes he played in the era. "As long as the NCAA doesn’t get the money, I like it," he said of athletes getting paid.

But the Hall of Famer is making up for lost time by investing in Joey nicotine pouches.

Joey has 36 different flavors, and Urlacher knows that the "pouch space as blown up."

"Everyone I play golf with, everyone I’m around, they’re always switching out these pouch things. I had a chance to invest, and it was a no-brainer for me," he said. They sent me the deck, and I was like, 'This seems like a home run.'

"It’s definitely safer than smoking or doing the vape stuff, because they don’t know the long-term effects of vaping," he said, expressing his personal opinion. "But the thing that’s crazy is how fast it’s caught on. Everyone does them. My daughter brings her friends over, and all three of them take them. I’m like, 'Whoa, she does them, too.' You can’t tell. They’re in their mouths. I’m like, 'Damn, everyone’s doing these — girls, guys.' The younger generations are really big on them. But I think I notice it the most when I play golf and every guy in my group is changing one every three holes. I’m like, 'Damn, these are a big deal.'"

Although the FDA has authorized nicotine pouch products for sale in the U.S., health experts warn against the effects they can have, particularly on younger people. A recent nationwide study published in the American Journal of Ophthalmology also suggested that smokeless alternatives could increase the risk of serious eye diseases compared to quitting nicotine altogether.
