item.title: Reporter's Notebook: Rand Paul's contempt vote crusade could be doomed despite Fauci pleading Fifth 111 times
item.description: Rand Paul plans a committee vote to hold Anthony Fauci in contempt of Congress after he invoked the Fifth Amendment 111 times during testimony.
item.content:encoded:
Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee Chairman Rand Paul, R-Ky., will schedule a committee vote next week to hold Anthony Fauci in contempt of Congress after invoking the Fifth Amendment 111 times today.

The committee could vote to hold Fauci in contempt. But it doesn’t stop there.

Contempt of Congress must go before the entire Senate. It takes a simple majority to hold someone in contempt. But such a resolution must clear one filibuster, requiring 60 yeas.

WATCH: FAUCI ATTORNEY EJECTED FROM SENATE HEARING AFTER CHAOTIC EXCHANGE: 'YOU ARE NOT RECOGNIZED!'

So, it’s doubtful Fauci is held in contempt.

Even if the Senate broke the filibuster, the Senate must approve a separate resolution to make a criminal referral to Department of Justice.

That would face at least one filibuster, again entailing 60 affirmative votes.

It is more common for the House to hold someone in contempt compared to the Senate. The Senate last successfully held someone in contempt in 1971.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Resurfaced video shows James Talarico discussing ‘exciting’ opportunity to end ‘over-policing’
item.description: Resurfaced video shows James Talarico calling efforts to end over-policing "really exciting" after 2020 Black Lives Matter riots in Austin, Texas.
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE: A resurfaced video shows that following the 2020 Black Lives Matter riots in the wake of George Floyd’s death, now-Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico said the country was facing a "really exciting" opportunity to "end the current situation of over-policing communities of color which has been in place in this country since its founding."

Talarico, a Texas state lawmaker, is tied in recent polling with Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton in the race to be the state's next U.S. senator. Such a flip would be the first in decades and would deal a major blow to the GOP's chances of retaining a Senate majority. Despite a history of controversial statements, including calling God nonbinary and claiming there are six genders, Talarico has recently positioned himself as a moderate, pro-police candidate.

However, critics are calling his pro-police stance into question after they say the resurfaced video destroys that narrative.

Zach Kraft, a spokesperson for the Republican National Committee, ripped Talarico as a "dangerous freak who is willing to endanger the entire state just to prove that he is sufficiently woke."

FAR-LEFT SENATE HOPEFUL EXPLAINS ‘OGRE ON A PIKE’ REMARK AFTER GETTING TORCHED BY HIS OWN PARTY

Kraft alleged that "James Talarico's wacked out vision for Texas with no police, no prisons, and no borders would put families in danger and be a paradise for criminal illegal aliens."

Unearthed clips from a September 2020 Zoom with South Asian American Voter Empowerment (SAAVETX) show Talarico saying that policymakers need to "listen to black voices and to the activists in the streets calling for a radically different vision of public safety."

He ripped Republicans who he accused of wanting to "scare white people to win an election," saying that "is a time-honored tradition in the Republican Party."

Talarico asserted that "police violence against communities of color, in particular our black community is nothing new, and has its roots in slavery and Jim Crow and mass incarceration."

He added that "this is just the latest iteration of the history of oppression this country has been a part of against African Americans."

Meanwhile, he said he would like to gather people "from activists and advocates to community leaders to law enforcement officials themselves to have a genuine discussion about what true public safety policy looks like and how we can end the current situation of over-policing communities of color which has been in place in this country since its founding."

He added that the discussion should be about "how do we take our criminal justice system at the state level, at the national level, and how do we make some fundamental changes to reflect our highest ideals and to really embody the country and state and the community that we want in the race to be."

"That’s taking place," he continued, adding that communities are "figuring out how we reinvest our limited public funding into these community-based solutions that really start to address the underlying causes of our criminal justice system attempts to treat."

"That to me is really exciting," he said.

DSA CO-CHAIR EMBRACES ABOLISHING SENATE, ICE, BORDERS AS DEMOCRATIC INFIGHTING ESCALATES

Talarico proceeded to say, "I applaud our local leaders that are trying to do that." He cited the city of Austin, which had recently approved a budget that cut tens of millions of dollars from the Austin Police Department. He ripped Republican Gov. Greg Abbott for having "proposed removing some of the revenue streams from cities like Austin because they’ve made local decisions for their local community."

At the time, Abbott released a statement saying that "Austin's decision puts the brave men and women of the Austin Police Department and their families at greater risk, and paves the way for lawlessness." The governor promised financial penalties for any Texas city defunding its police force, saying, "Public safety is job one, and Austin has abandoned that duty."

During the Zoom call, however, Talarico asserted that for Abbott to "complain about local communities not funding public safety is hypocritical."

"To see the governor continue to try to undermine our local governments, I think is rich to say the least," he said.

In response to the new criticism, JT Ennis, a spokesperson for Talarico’s campaign, told Fox News Digital that "James opposes defunding the police, has voted to deny bail for violent criminals, and has a record of sending billions of dollars to support law enforcement."

Additionally, Ennis said that Talarico "supports a secure southern border and has unveiled a border security agenda backed by law enforcement officials from both parties."

Meanwhile, he accused Paxton of having "abused his office to benefit his wealthy donors and the well-connected, allowing criminals back on the street even as it made Texans less safe," adding, "Even Ken Paxton’s fellow Republicans have blasted his public safety record: more murders, soft on human trafficking, and pedophiles walking free."

MAINE’S NEW DEMOCRATIC SENATE NOMINEE, TROY JACKSON, TELLS FOX NEWS DIGITAL ‘I’VE BEEN VETTED’

Ennis has previously called the assertion that Talarico is pro-defund the police a "flat out lie."

He said that previous legislation proposed by Talarico "supports the police by adding desperately needed mental health officials to help prevent tragic events like the mass shooting at Robb Elementary in Uvalde, Texas."

Madison Cercy, a spokesperson for Paxton's campaign, said that "James Talarico has the most consistently anti-law enforcement record in the Texas Legislature. But now his spokesman is out telling bold-faced lies."

"For his campaign to even insinuate that Talarico has, at any point in his career, 'stood with law enforcement' is one of the most egregious lies they have told throughout this campaign," Cercy told Fox News Digital.

She said that Talarico "donated thousands of dollars to an organization that supported defunding the police and voted against banning personal bond release for people accused of violent crimes," while emphasizing that "just because he votes on a basic spending bill like every other state representative does not mean he has ever 'supported law enforcement.'"

"If it were up to Talarico," she continued, "We would hand over our communities to the radicals who pillaged our streets during the 2020 defund the police movement and let criminals out of prison in pursuit of a socialist agenda."

item.title: Hawley trolls Fauci's blanket Fifth Amendment claims exposing 'contempt for this body'
item.description: Anthony Fauci invoked his Fifth Amendment right dozens of times, refusing to answer even what day it was or what color his tie was at the hearing.
item.content:encoded:
Former NIAID Director Anthony Fauci’s refusal to answer questions from Congress extended to simple facts, including the day of the week and the color of the tie he was wearing.

Fauci, 85, invoked his Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination about as many times as his years alive on Earth, despite Senate Homeland Security and Government Affairs Committee Chairman Rand Paul, R-Ky., and Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., asserting that he did not have that right given his current legal status.

Hawley cited a Supreme Court case from 1896, where President Benjamin Harrison’s appointee, Justice Henry Brown, ruled that a witness granted statutory immunity from prosecution could nonetheless be compelled to testify because his immunity displaced pleading the Fifth.

FAUCI PLEADS FIFTH WITH 'ZERO LEGAL JUSTIFICATION' AS CRITICS ERUPT AND DEMAND CONTEMPT CHARGES

In that case, an auditor for a Pittsburgh railroad unsuccessfully challenged a contempt charge for refusing to answer grand jury questions.

Hawley turned to Fauci and tested his repeated Fifth Amendment invocations throughout the hearing, quipping, "Doc, let’s try something."

"What day of the week is it today?" Hawley asked Wednesday.

Fauci replied with his boilerplate invocation of the Fifth Amendment.

"What color tie are you wearing?" Hawley asked.

Fauci declined to answer, again invoking the Fifth Amendment.

‘PRIVILEGED’ HUNTER BIDEN, SPARED BY DAD’S PARDON, BLASTS TRUMP’S CLEMENCY POWER

"Let's just get one thing straight. You don't have any rights under the Fifth Amendment because you've been pardoned, as you very well know," he said, invoking the 1896 Brown v. Walker case.

Hawley, who is also an attorney, added that the legal reality was likely why Fauci’s remaining attorneys were "shifting nervously" behind him.

A top Fauci attorney, David Schertler, had previously been ejected by Paul after refusing to take his assigned seat and remain quiet.

"This isn't about the law. This is about contempt, contempt for this body and contempt for the American people," Hawley said.

"But I think I know why you're doing it. It's because you don't want to answer questions. It's because you did all kinds of terrible things. It's because during the pandemic, you got rich… while people were dying."

WATCH: FAUCI ATTORNEY EJECTED FROM SENATE HEARING AFTER CHAOTIC EXCHANGE: ‘YOU ARE NOT RECOGNIZED!’

Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, followed Hawley with similar questions that Fauci refused to answer.

Moreno said Fauci should know what the Fifth Amendment is if he wanted to invoke it dozens of times.

When he asked Fauci to recite the Fifth Amendment, Fauci invoked his Fifth Amendment right.

"No, I’m just asking you what it says," Moreno repeated.

"On the advice of counsel, I respectfully decline to answer based upon my rights under the Fifth Amendment to the Constitution," Fauci said once more.

Moreno then gave a copy of the Constitution to an aide and instructed him to bring it to Fauci to read.

That attempt also prompted the same repeated response from the octogenarian immunologist.

"So you're invoking a right that you don't know who wrote it or what it says? Is that correct?" Moreno quipped.

Fauci again invoked his Fifth Amendment right after declining to recite the amendment when asked.

Fox News anchor Harris Faulkner later discussed the legal implications of Fauci's repeated Fifth Amendment invocations.

She cited President Joe Biden’s blanket, retroactive pardon against Fauci, saying that he is "protected from any offenses against the United States he may have taken part in."

Faulkner said the pardon does not cover state criminal prosecutions, future crimes or congressional investigations.

"It does not protect him from prosecution from perjury if he lies under oath after receiving the pardon," she said.

item.title: Coffee slushie is summer's hottest drink but expert warns one mistake can turn it 'into more of a dessert'
item.description: The viral coffee slushie trend works with cold brew or hot coffee, but a dietitian warns flavored syrups can quietly turn it into a dessert.
item.content:encoded:
Coffee lovers have found their latest summer obsession: the coffee slushie.

The icy drink has been making the rounds on social media, with home baristas freezing brewed coffee before blending it into a frosty, caffeine-packed treat.

While the frozen beverage looks indulgent, experts say the drink itself isn't necessarily any less healthy than your usual cup of joe. Rather, it all depends on what you add to it.

SCIENTISTS USED ELECTRICITY ON COFFEE AND DISCOVERED WHAT MAKES IT TASTE GOOD

"Honestly, the frozen format itself doesn't make coffee any more or less healthy than drinking it hot," South Carolina-based dietitian nutritionist Lauren Manaker told Fox News Digital. "It's still just coffee, just colder and more fun for summer."

In fact, a homemade coffee slushie can be a smarter choice than other frozen beverages, Manaker said.

"A homemade coffee slushie can actually be a healthier option, since traditional slushies are typically loaded with added sugars and offer little nutritional value," she said.

To make the drink more satisfying, she recommends using dairy milk.

"Opting for dairy milk brings a unique combination of 13 essential nutrients and quality protein together that can help you feel more satiated, all with no added sugars," Manaker said. "If you're lactose intolerant, lactose-free dairy milk is a great option that keeps those same nutritional benefits intact, just without the lactose."

The biggest nutritional pitfall isn't the coffee but the extras, Manaker cautioned.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"Flavored syrups, sweetened creamers and sugary toppings are what can quietly turn your everyday iced coffee into more of a dessert," she said.

Chandra Holt, the Texas-based founder of Incredibrew, said coffee naturally lends itself to the frozen format.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"A cup of coffee is 95% water, so if you freeze it, you don't need to add ice, so it makes a great slushie," she said, adding that the recipe works with either cold brew or hot coffee that's been cooled before freezing.

For the best flavor, Holt recommends brewing a stronger batch.

"The key is using strong coffee so you get a lot of coffee flavor after you add the milk," she noted.

item.title: NCAA suspends Tennessee linebacker for $427 plane ticket, as college sports hands out millions in NIL
item.description: Tennessee's Arion Carter returned from injury to play college football, but the NCAA suspended him two games for accepting a flight from an NFL agent.
item.content:encoded:
The NCAA has lost another battle in the court of public opinion, and this time it involves a college football player at Tennessee.

In a world in which college athletes are being paid millions of dollars to play, it looks as though the NCAA is still harping on the small things like we are still living in the past. Should this come as a surprise? Probably not, given the organization is still trying to hold onto any power they have left within this current ecosystem of college athletics.

Tennessee linebacker Arion Carter has been suspended two games by the NCAA for accepting a flight paid for by an NFL agent after he decided that he would try his hand at professional football after the 2025 season and signed with representation.

Tick Tock: SEC and Big Ten receive revised Protect College Sports Act as Senate vote timeline looms

How much was the plane ticket? A measly $427 that only came when Carter decided to enter the 2026 NFL Draft. This violation, which is a Level III, is pretty far down the totem pole when it comes to NCAA standards on rules.

But, because Carter had accepted this travel from a professional agent, compared to the hundreds of NIL or college agents that are roaming throughout college athletics, it doesn’t matter that Arion had repaid the $427 earlier this year.

Yes, you read that right. In a world in which much more egregious rules will be broken on a random Tuesday, Carter is being punished for signing with an NFL agent and accepting an airline ticket.

Don't get me wrong, I understand the NCAA has a rule that says if a player declares for the draft and signs with an agent, he cannot return to the collegiate ranks.

But, these were uncharted waters, given Arion Carter was hurt very early in the process, and did the smart thing by returning to college.

It wasn’t as if he waited until three weeks before the NFL Draft. In reality, there needs to be a process for players to return if something like this happens. Carter wasn’t chasing a lucrative bag, given that he had already declared and Tennessee even announced his intentions.

COLLEGE SPORTS SEES PIVOTAL MOMENT AS SENATE LOOKS TO MOVE LEGISLATION ON NIL, TRANSFERS ACROSS GOAL LINE

We have athletes that have played professional baseball for ten years currently on rosters in college football.

But, the NCAA draws the line and also states he should actually be indefinitely suspended, so they are doing Carter a favor by only handing down a 2-game judgement (after they initially wanted 3 games).

After declaring for the NFL Draft, the Tennessee linebacker started the process of working out in preparation for his professional career. It was during one of those workouts where Arion Carter suffered an injury that forced him to make a decision about whether he should return for one more season of college football.

Ultimately, he decided to take his name out of the NFL Draft process and return to Tennessee for the upcoming season.

At last week's SEC Media Days in Tampa, Carter represented the Vols and had this to say about returning to Tennessee after a setback.

"Coming back off my injury and ultimately choosing to come back to the University of Tennessee was a pivotal point in my life. I fell like I made the greatest decision I possibly could have made," Carter told reporters.

Somewhere in the realm of college athletics at this moment, there is a player cashing a check from a university or third-party collective that is in the five- to six-figure range.

That's the world we live in now, where even high school athletes are being promised private-jet hours to entice them to sign with a school. Heck, there are schools offering athletes actual real estate property for future investments to sign with a college.

Inside the fight: NIL arms race fueling new push for College Football Playoff expansion

Have I mentioned that athletes are making seven-figures a year to play sports at the collegiate level?

"This is ridiculous, if that's exactly how it played out," one Power-4 general manger told OutKick-FOX News. "I just had a player in my office looking for a $30,000 raise before we start Fall camp, and the NCAA is punishing a player for making the right decision when it comes to his long-term viability when trying to play football.

"What are we doing? Look, I usually have zero sympathy for an opposing school we're competing with for players, but I feel horrible for the young man."

Did the NCAA take on Tennessee this aggressively because of past litigation? I mean, possibly, given that the Vols essentially sued the organization in order to steer them away from potential penalties related to the recruitment of Nico Iamaleava years ago.

Sure, there could be pettiness involved here. Or, the NCAA is once again trying to puff their chests out to send a message that they are still in charge of rules and penalties.

Personally, I'm going with the second option.

A resurfaced video of Dr. Anthony Fauci's 2021 door-to-door COVID-19 vaccine campaign is gaining renewed attention amid his contentious testimony before Congress on the federal handling of the pandemic.

The clip shows Fauci, then White House health advisor, and Washington, D.C., Mayor Muriel Bowser visiting residents in the city's Anacostia neighborhood to encourage them to get vaccinations. But the footage shows several skeptical residents challenging Fauci over the vaccines' rapid development, long-term safety and the government's messaging — exchanges that have become a flashpoint in the debate over the federal response.

And now that Fauci's diary has been published and includes seemingly contradictory public statements versus private musings, his entire involvement has come under the microscope of his biggest critics.

"The people in America are not settled with the information that's been given to us right now. So I'm not gonna be lining up taking a shot on a vaccination, for something that wasn't clear in the first place, and then you all create a shot in miraculous time. It takes years to create," said a Washington, D.C. resident in the video shot by PBS in response to Fauci's vaccine push campaign.

DID THE BIDEN ADMINISTRATION PURPOSEFULLY IGNORE COVID VACCINE SIDE EFFECTS?

Fauci and Bowser, who is leaving office at the conclusion of her current term, encouraged residents in the "historic African American neighborhood" of D.C. to get the vaccine, seemingly attempting to persuade skeptical residents and using Fauci as an expert to sway them.

"[If] thousands of people, like you, don't get vaccinated, you're going to let this virus continue to percolate in this country and in this world," urged Bowser, standing alongside the nation's top voice on the coronavirus at the time.

That resident pushed back, continuing to question the very swift timeline of the vaccine's development and roll out. They compared it to the flu and expressed skepticism over why the government was incentivizing residents to get the jab.

FAUCI PRIVATELY TOOK CREDIT FOR COVID-19 LOCKDOWNS DESPITE PUBLIC DENIAL, NEWLY EXPOSED DIARY ENTRIES REVEAL

"Because when you start talking about paying people to get vaccinated, when you start talking about incentivizing things to get people vaccinated, there's something else going on with that. Something else. It's something else," said the resident.

Critics on social media swiftly responded to the resurfaced clip.

"They're terrified of a free-thinking black man. God bless this man," wrote "The Riley Gaines Show" podcast Riley Gaines on X.

"Earlier this day, Fauci learned he had a blood clot in his lung. Yet he still beat on black people’s doors, telling them to get the COVID shots. And these (mad) scientists wonder why black Americans are leery of vaccines? Maybe they don’t want to be Tuskegee test rats again," wrote Article III Project founder Mike Davis.

EXCLUSIVE: BIDEN PARDON WON'T SHIELD FAUCI IF HE LIES TO CONGRESS, COMER SAYS

"Never forget this brave American citizen that turned down getting a Covid vaccine and called out Fauci right to his face on camera," wrote one user on X.

"What an absolute legend this guy… telling that narcissistic, deranged liar and his acolytes to GFT with their sh*tccine," wrote Bitcoin miner Javier Hermonsa.

Fauci and Bowser both did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment on the video making its rounds on social media ahead of the retired medical advisor's appearance in Congress on Wednesday.

Fauci was subpoenaed by Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee Chairman Sen. Rand Paul to answer questions primarily about the U.S. government's handling of COVID-19 and the origins of the virus.

Ahead of the hearing Wednesday morning, President Donald Trump blasted Fauci on Truth Social.

"I Inherited Fauci, who was there since the 1980’s, but with each passing day, relied less and less on him. He made too many bad calls," wrote Trump in part.

"Fauci was largely taken out of play, and then along came Sleepy Joe Biden, who made Fauci a ‘King!’ I called Biden to tell him Fauci was no good, either didn’t have a clue, or was dishonest. The call was well received, but sadly, not acted on. Biden went on to give Fauci vast destructive power," he added.

During the hearing, Fauci repeatedly refused to answer substantive questions, invoking the Fifth Amendment against questions from lawmakers at least 111 times during the hearing.

Paul said the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs will hold a vote next week to "certify" Fauci's contempt of Congress.

item.title: The Nintendo 64 is turning 30 years old, here are some of its most impactful games of all time
item.description: From "Goldeneye 007" to "Ocarina of Time," the N64 turns 30 this summer. These five games defined 3D gaming and still shape the industry today.
item.content:encoded:
If you don't want to feel old, I'd suggest you click away from this article now, but the Nintendo 64 is celebrating its 30th birthday this summer (I warned you).

The console that helped usher 3D gaming into homes everywhere and catapulted us into the fifth generation of gaming has had plenty of legacy-defining games attached to its name.

Today, I want to honor the N64 turning the big 3-0 by looking at some of the most impactful games that were ever released on the console.

Full disclosure, this isn't a "favorites" list.

Some of my favorite and most-played N64 games might not make the list, and there might be a game or two on here that I don't necessarily love.

'HALO' COMPOSER RUNNING FOR CONGRESS DRAWS PARALLELS TO DECLINE OF WOKENESS IN GAMING TO TRUMP'S RE-ELECTION

Conversely, your favorite game might get left off the list, so if that's the case, be sure to scream at me about it in the comments section.

Without further ado, let's talk video games.

We kick this list off with an absolute banger, although, let's be honest, they're all bangers.

"Goldeneye 007" is widely considered one of the most revolutionary first person shooters in gaming history.

The 1997 James Bond movie tie-in took what games like "Doom" and "Wolfenstein" did and brought it into the next generation of gaming.

The gameplay was mind-blowing, especially for the time, but the thing that separated "Goldeneye" from its peers was the multiplayer.

Its four-player "couch multiplayer" set the standard for shooters to come and was so ahead of its time that college dorm rooms still frequent it to this day.

A special mention has to be made to the soundtrack, which has gained an almost cult-like following from both nostalgic Millennials and newer Gen Z fans alike.

If you want an idea of just how impactful a game has become, you'll notice "high-definition remakes" start to pop up years after its release.

"Star Fox 64" is no different, as it has a brand-spanking-new remake out on the Switch 2 nearly three decades after the original.

As far as the N64 version of this game is concerned, there's a reason people have been clamoring for a remake of this game since 1997.

The story of ace pilot Fox McCloud and his misfit crew of anthropomorphic sidekicks has white-knuckle dogfighting, a fun and tightly packed campaign, and more memorable quotes than you could find in any modern movie.

MADDEN 27'S TUSH PUSH TEASE HIGHLIGHTS EVERYTHING WRONG WITH ANNUALLY RELEASED SPORTS GAMES

Seriously, this game spawned the "do a barrel roll" meme that swept the internet in the late 2000s and early 2010s, almost 15 years after the game came out.

If you were looking for a fun crossover between "Star Wars" and "Independence Day" mixed with fun and goofy humor, this was your bag.

Before 1999, the thought of all your favorite video game characters beating the tar out of each other on the same video game console felt like a pipe dream.

That's why "Super Smash Bros." was so Earth-shattering upon its release. It gave every fan something they didn't even know they wanted and set the bar in the process.

Manufacturing a scenario where Link, Samus, Mario, and Fox McCloud could all fight to the death on some of the most iconic Nintendo stages felt like a fever dream.

There were bonus stages, unlockables, and achievements galore, which for the fifth generation of consoles was far ahead of its time.

"Super Smash Bros." created a template for all games to follow after and yet is so unique that it still hasn't been properly imitated or duplicated since.

A true original like this deserves a seat at the table on this list.

The game that started it all, "Super Mario 64" was, surprisingly enough, a launch title for the N64.

Amazingly, one of the best and most impactful games Nintendo has ever created was also the first to be released on their fifth-gen console.

The pairing of Nintendo's most legendary mascot coupled with their first jump into the realm of 3D alone makes this an instant classic, but "Super Mario 64" is more than that.

Every 3D platformer you've ever played owes its very existence to "Super Mario 64," and even 30 years later, the game still holds up.

The soundtrack is iconic, the gameplay is fluid and responsive and rewards skilled players, and there were so many secrets to be found that Easter egg hunters are still discovering bits, pieces, and oddities to this day.

If you haven't experienced "Super Mario 64" for yourself, give it a try.

I promise you won't be disappointed.

Here it is, the granddaddy of them all.

You knew it was going to end up on this list, as it routinely ends up on plenty of "greatest of all time" lists and sits comfortably atop the Metacritic rankings, but it's more than just numbers for "Ocarina of Time."

The game introduced a huge and expansive overworld map, a timeless story, and gameplay mechanics that set the bar for all 3D action-adventure games to come.

If you don't believe me, just look up "Z-Targeting."

The creators of "Ocarina of Time" literally invented a lock-on mechanic to help with 3D sword combat that every game since then has emulated in one way or another.

You want a memorable cast of characters? Check.

How about an iconic soundtrack? Check plus.

No game will ever be able to replicate the sense of wonder "Ocarina of Time" created upon its release, and we as gamers have been chasing that high ever since.

Sure, games like "Breath of the Wild" have come close, but it will never feel the same as the first time we popped that golden cartridge into our N64's and stepped out into Hyrule Field for the first time.

Happy birthday, Nintendo 64! Thanks for the memories.
